title: The Timeline revamp PR added IssueBulkUpdateDateEndpoint, which fetches issues by caller-supplied ids without filtering by the URL's workspace and project, so a member of any project can change start/target dates of any issue on the instance.

findings.explanation: The PR adds workspace and project scoping filters to the Issue query at line 1121, which is a security fix. However, this fix is being applied to code that was previously vulnerable. The base version at line 1121 (before the PR) fetched issues with only `Issue.objects.filter(id__in=issue_ids)` without any workspace or project scoping, allowing any authenticated user with ADMIN or MEMBER role in ANY project to fetch and bulk update issues from OTHER workspaces/projects by ID. The @allow_permission decorator at line 1113 validates the user has the required role in the specific workspace/project (via kwargs['slug'] and kwargs['project_id']), but the data query was not respecting these scoping constraints. The PR correctly fixes this by adding `workspace__slug=slug, project_id=project_id` filters, but the base code represents a classic IDOR vulnerability where object access was not scoped to the authorized context.

evidence.content: The decorator validates that the request.user has the required role in the specific workspace (slug) and project (project_id). The endpoint-level authorization check creates a contract that data queries must also be scoped to the authorized workspace/project context.

findings.suggested_fix: The PR correctly applies workspace and project scoping filters to the Issue query. Ensure all bulk operations and data access follow this pattern of filtering by both workspace__slug and project_id when the decorator validates access at that level.
